newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, no changes foreseen.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, no changes foreseen.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in Wednesday's moderate trade and market participants foresaw no significant shifts in prices before the Easter holidays.
Fully listed drug firm Pliva took the spotlight as the leading gainer and the most active issue adding 20 kuna, or 4.7 percent, to 450 kuna on volume of 4,661 shares.
It's Global Depository Receits which represent 1/5 of each share rose to $14.97 from $14.63 on Tuesday.

"High demand has obviously something to do with optimistic expectations of Pliva's business results," Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage told Reuters. Pliva is due to publish its 1996 results in April.
But Nikolac said its price should see no further growth before a rise in London. "Last week the diffrence between Zagreb and London was up to 30 kuna and now it has almost completely melted away."
Another blue chip Zagrebacka Banka closed ten kuna higher at 1,850 after trading in 1,801-1865 kuna range with 927 units changing hands.
Six of 12 active issues fell, five rose and one was flat.
Volume shrank to 7,974 units and turnover was halved at 4.9 million kuna.
Food company Podravka edged down 4.5 kuna to 295, five kuna below what analysts perceive as its rock bottom, with 1,432 units sold.

"I expect it at least to hold at this level, without a further plunge," Nikolac said. Podravka is among 800 companies included in voucher privatisation scheme whose assets are to be distributed among refugees and war victims.
Many local shareholders were worried about the effect this might have on their investment and pushed to sell, analysts said.

The voucher privatisation will have no real impact on the market before autumn, but Podravka's plunge was the first reaction after the list of companies included in the scheme was published earlier this month, Nikolac said.
Hotelier Suncani Hvar led the losers, slipping three kuna to 63 kuna on volume of 276 units.
Laguna, in which foreign investors have a large stake, was the only hotelier that escaped general slide of tourist shares, adding 40 kuna to 1,455 kuna with 220 units sold.
